inline_comments.comment: The `renderer` variable holds the full npm package name (e.g., `@storybook/react`), so this template produces an invalid import path like `@storybook/@storybook/react`. You need to extract just the short renderer name. One safe approach is: `const rendererShortName = (projectInfo.renderer ?? 'react').split('/').pop() ?? 'react';` and then use `rendererShortName` in the import template instead of `renderer`.

When the framework is not `@storybook/react-vite`, the function returns silently with no output and no explanation. A user running `storybook ai init` on a Next.js or Angular project will see nothing and have no idea why. This should log a clear, actionable message such as `logger.warn('storybook ai init currently only supports @storybook/react-vite projects.')` before returning. Silently no-opping is especially confusing since the command exits with code 0.

This `logger.log('Detecting agent presence: ...')` fires unconditionally, even when no agent is detected—logging `Detecting agent presence: undefined` for every user who runs `npx create storybook`. This is clearly a debugging artifact and must be removed before merging. The subsequent log inside `if (isAgent)` already provides the user-facing message.

This uses a deep relative path into another package's source directory (`../../cli-storybook/src/ai`), and `cli-storybook` is not declared as a dependency in `create-storybook/package.json`. This means the import bypasses the package's public API surface and relies on the relative file system layout being stable. Per project convention, cross-package imports should go through the public package export (e.g., `import { aiInit } from '@storybook/cli-storybook/ai'` or equivalent), with `cli-storybook` added to `create-storybook`'s `dependencies`.

The generated decorator example uses JSX syntax (`<ThemeProvider>`, `<Story />`) but instructs the AI agent to place this code in `preview.ts` (a plain TypeScript file). JSX is not valid in `.ts` files—it requires a `.tsx` extension. The code example and the filename reference in the instructions (also at line 163 for the non-factory branch) should say `preview.tsx`. This would cause agents to produce a config file that fails to compile.

The project rule for `code/lib/**` is to use `logger` from `storybook/internal/node-logger` instead of `console.*`. Even though the comment notes this is 'for machine consumption', the `logger` utility can be configured to write to stdout. If `console.log` is intentional here for machine-parseable output that must not be mixed with log-level formatting, add an explicit comment explaining that deviation from the project convention.

`detectAgent()` is called three times: once at module load to compute `isAgent`, once for the unconditional log at this line, and once again inside the `if (isAgent)` block. Since `isAgent` is already computed from the first call, `detectAgent().name` should be stored as a `const agentName = detectAgent().name` (or derived from `isAgent`) so the detection logic doesn't run repeatedly.

The comment on this exported type property should be a JSDoc block comment (`/** Whether this is being run via an AI agent */`) rather than a line comment (`//`), so IDE hover tooltips are populated and the documentation is consistent with other type properties in this file.

The CSF Factory story format example instructs the AI agent to use `import { config } from '#.storybook/preview'`. This is a Node.js subpath import that requires an `imports` field in the project's `package.json` pointing to `.storybook/preview`. The generated instructions don't tell the agent to verify or configure this prerequisite. If subpath imports are not configured, the generated stories will fail to resolve the import at runtime.

`storiesPaths: string[]` is collected and stored in `ProjectInfo`, but it is never referenced in `prompt.ts`'s generated markdown or JSON output. If it is unused at this stage, it adds dead weight to the type and the data pipeline. Either use it in the instructions (e.g., show the agent the actual story glob patterns from the config) or remove it from `ProjectInfo` until it is needed.

`projectInfo.renderer` is typed as `string | null`. Using `||` here means an empty string would also fall back to `'react'`, whereas `??` would only fall back for `null` and `undefined`. Since the value is always set to `data.rendererPackage ?? 'unknown'` in `aiInit`, it can never be `null` at this call site—but the type still permits it. Prefer `projectInfo.renderer ?? 'react'` to match the declared type and make intent explicit.

general_comments.comment: The `storybook ai init` command silently produces no output for any framework other than `@storybook/react-vite`. Given the PR description frames this as a general AI initialization feature, this is a significant undocumented limitation. Users on Next.js, Angular, Svelte, or any other framework will run the command and see nothing. At minimum, the command's description string should note it is react-vite only, and the guard should log a clear, user-facing message explaining what's unsupported and what might be coming. Alternatively, if broader framework support is not part of this PR's scope, the design should be reconsidered before merging.

The previous `storybook skill` command (removed in this PR) had its implementation explicitly stubbed out with a TODO comment and its telemetry call commented out. This PR replaces it with a working `storybook ai init` command, which is good—but the old `skill` command removal should be confirmed as safe: check that no external documentation, scripts, or CI references `storybook skill`. A search in the repo and a note in MIGRATION.md would ensure users who relied on the stub are aware of the rename to `storybook ai init`.

The new `detect-agent.ts` file in `create-storybook` duplicates agent-detection logic that already exists in `code/core/src/telemetry/detect-agent.ts`. The PR should use the existing canonical telemetry utility rather than creating a parallel implementation in a different package. If the existing utility doesn't cover the new agents (Claude Code SSE port, Copilot, Cline, etc.), those additions should be contributed upstream to the core `detect-agent.ts` and then imported from there, not maintained as a separate copy.

Neither the new `code/lib/cli-storybook/src/ai/` module nor `code/lib/create-storybook/src/bin/detect-agent.ts` include any automated tests (the PR checklist confirms no tests were added). Core logic like `getDocsUrl`, `parseMajorVersion`, `getCsfExample`, and `detectAgent` are straightforward to unit-test. In particular, the renderer-name interpolation bug described in the inline comments would have been caught by a test asserting `getCsfExample('@storybook/react')` does not contain `@storybook/@storybook/react`.

The `getPreviewConfigExample` function generates code examples showing JSX in `preview.ts` (both the CSF Factory and the CSF3 variants). The heading in Step 2 of the instructions also says `Configure preview.ts`. Since the decorator examples universally require JSX, all references should instruct the agent to use `preview.tsx`. The mismatch between the filename and its content will cause the agent to produce a non-compiling config file.
